item: chaos coverage for the money path
not_deployed: disposable PostgreSQL and Kafka on random ports, plus an in-process catalog stub; no project volume or Compose service is touched
why_these_faults_together: A database outage or read-only database must stop checkout: the dangerous answer is a 2xx carrying an order id for a row that was never written. A broker outage must NOT stop checkout: the outbox exists so Kafka is not a hard dependency of taking money.

observations.baseline: 201 with the order persisted as PAID
observations.postgresql_paused: 500, and the order count was unchanged afterwards, so the failed attempt left no phantom row
observations.postgresql_read_only: the database continued accepting connections and SELECTs, checkout returned 500, and the order count stayed unchanged
observations.kafka_paused: 201: checkout completed with the broker down
observations.after_kafka_returned: the outbox drained without a restart

defects_found_in_the_drill_itself: The catalog stub served only the product-snapshot GET, but checkout also reserves stock with POST /api/v1/internal/inventory/products/{id}/decrement before it charges. Every reservation failed, so every order took the compensation path -- which from outside is indistinguishable from a payment failure.

The baseline accepted any 2xx. The controller answers 202 for PENDING_PAYMENT and COMPENSATING, so a checkout that never completed passed the baseline, and the later outbox assertions were then examining an order that was never placed. Checks 1 and 4 now require 201 specifically, and check 1 asserts a PAID row exists. An assertion loose enough for a broken setup to pass is the same class of error as measuring a stale artifact.
The jar-freshness check watched all of src, so a change to a test file forced a rebuild. Scoped to src/main, which is what actually ends up in the jar.
what_this_does_not_cover: The read-only case covers a live database that rejects writes. Disk-full behavior, packet loss, and progressively slow responses remain untested.
The payment provider is the in-process mock, so no real provider timeout or decline is exercised here.
catalog-service is a stub serving the agreed contract fixture, not the real service.
